title: World Cup 2026 Final: Argentina Face Spain as Messi Chases Mbappe for Golden Boot
excerpt: The biggest match in football kicks off today in East Rutherford as Messi bids for a record third Golden Ball and England claim third place with a wild 6-4 win over France.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Argentina faces Spain in the 2026 FIFA World Cup Final today at 3:00 PM ET.
  • Kylian Mbappé leads the Golden Boot race, with Messi needing a strong final to overtake him.
  • England secured third place with a thrilling 6-4 victory over France, their best finish since 1966.
  • Messi, at age 39, may play his final World Cup match, adding historic significance to the final.
  • Argentina take on Spain in the 2026 FIFA World Cup Final today at the New York New Jersey Stadium in East Rutherford, kicking off at 3:00 PM ET / 12:00 PM PT.
  • Kylian Mbappé leads the Golden Boot race, with Lionel Messi trailing and needing a big final to overtake him; Messi is in contention for a record third Golden Ball.
  • England claimed third place on Saturday with a stunning 6-4 victory over France, scoring four goals in the first half before withstanding a French comeback.
  • The final could be Messi’s last World Cup match at age 39, adding historic weight to the occasion.

The 2026 FIFA World Cup reaches its climax today as Argentina face Spain at the New York New Jersey Stadium in East Rutherford — a final that could define the legacies of two generations of football superstars.

Kickoff is at 3:00 PM ET (12:00 PM PT), with the match broadcast on FOX in the United States and available on Peacock Premium, Telemundo, and Fubo TV.

The Golden Boot Race

The individual awards add another layer of drama to the final. Kylian Mbappé leads the Golden Boot race heading into the match, having piled up goals during France’s run to the semifinals before their defeat to England. Lionel Messi trails but has the advantage of one more game to play.

A big performance from Messi in the final could see him overtake Mbappé for the top scorer’s award. The Argentine also remains in strong contention for the Golden Ball, awarded to the tournament’s best player. Winning it would give Messi a record third Golden Ball, adding to the awards he received in 2014 and 2022.

England’s Wild Third-Place Win

Saturday’s third-place playoff delivered one of the most entertaining matches of the tournament. England demolished France 6-4 in Miami, racing to a 4-0 lead in the first half before the French mounted a furious second-half comeback, scoring four goals to briefly threaten an improbable equalization. England held firm, adding two more goals to clinch a commanding win.

The result gives England their best World Cup finish since winning the tournament in 1966, while France’s campaign ends in disappointment despite Mbappé’s prolific scoring.

Argentina’s Path to the Final

Argentina topped Group J with a perfect record of three wins from three matches, scoring nine points and looking dominant throughout the group stage. Their knockout run has been built on a blend of Messi’s creativity, clinical finishing, and a defense that has rarely looked troubled.

For Messi, 39, this is almost certainly his final World Cup. Having won the trophy in 2022 in Qatar, the opportunity to defend it on American soil — and potentially retire as a two-time champion — adds historic weight to every minute he plays today.

Spain’s Challenge

Spain, who topped Group H with seven points, have combined their trademark possession-based football with a new directness that has caught opponents off guard. Their path through the knockout stages demonstrated both tactical flexibility and the depth of their squad.

The European champions will be looking to add the World Cup to the European Championship they won last year, a double that only Spain (2010-2012) have achieved in the modern era.

A Tournament for the Ages

The 2026 World Cup, the first hosted across three countries (United States, Mexico, and Canada) and the first with 48 teams, has delivered record-breaking viewership, attendance, and ticket prices. The final is no exception — average seat costs have reached $11,327, shattering previous records.

For Indian fans in the United States, the tournament’s American venues have made it unusually accessible. Bollywood and cricket celebrities have been spotted at matches throughout the tournament, and MS Dhoni’s decade-old social media post appeared to have predicted the Spain-Argentina final, going viral this week.
